title: Bibliopolis world file
description: A world built by hand, as docs/world.md describes it: the rule it started with, the items that became houses, and the append-only log of events that the city is the fold of. This schema says the shape of the file. What it cannot say the program checks when it reads the file: an id used once among the events that count, events numbered 1, 2, 3, ... in order, min no more than max, an `items` list equal to the items of the add_item events, a topic not named twice by one item, whitespace-only text, and every refusal of the world (a house that is not there, a road that exists, a node that another road stands for, a road that holds `branches` roads already, a member of a merge that does not stand directly below its parent, a rule whose `branches` would leave a direction number or a road without its place, an undo that a later event depends on). A file that satisfies the schema may still be refused; a file that does not is always refused.

rule.description: The rule the world started with; a set_rule event changes it from its place in the log on.

items.description: The item of every add_item event, in log order (an undone one too): written from the events for a reader that does not fold.

events.description: The log, in order. seq runs 1, 2, 3, ...

text.description: Text without control characters: an id, or a name that is written into a place id.

count.description: A whole number, 1 or more (the program reads none above 10**12).

max.description: How many houses a road is meant to hold.

min.description: The least a new road takes. No more than max.

auto.description: Whether the rule acts by itself after each arrival.

branches.description: How many roads a road holds directly, and how many avenues leave the ring road.

rule.description: The rule of a set_rule event: every key is there.

start_rule.description: The rule a world starts with: branches may be left out, and is then 13.

openalex_topic.description: An OpenAlex topic with all four levels, the widest first.

id.description: Unique among the houses; the id of the house.

year.description: The year of publication, or null.

doi.description: Optional; null when there is none.

type.description: The kind of document, e.g. article, review, editorial.

openalex.description: Optional; the primary topic first, then up to two more. Empty or left out: no topic is known.

annex_of.description: Optional, and only with annex_form. The id of the house that this item exists for. Where that house stands on a lot, the item stands beside it at once and has no lot; where it has not arrived, the item is an ordinary house that waits and is absorbed when the house arrives.

annex_form.description: Optional, and only with annex_of. How the item stands beside its house: a wing on its side wall, or a mailbox at its gate.

id.description: The id of the OpenAlex node.

road_node.description: The OpenAlex node a road stands for, or null for a category the player named. Two roads never stand for one node.

moment.description: ISO 8601: a date, or a date and time with or without an offset. The fold writes it into the chronicle and never reads the clock.

payload.description: The item becomes a house on the ring road round the town hall.

road.description: The id of the new road: not of the form lane:<id>:<n>, not starting with auto:.

parent.description: The road to open below, or null for the ring road.

houses.description: The houses that move onto the road; they stand directly on the place it opens from.

road.description: The road to name, or null for the ring road.

parent.description: A road: a move never makes a ring-1 road.

road.description: The id of the new road: not of the form lane:<id>:<n>, not starting with auto:.

parent.description: The road the new road stands below, or null for the ring road (the new road is then an avenue).

members.description: The roads that stand directly below parent and stand below the new road: a new avenue takes the direction of the one with the widest sector, the others' are free.

seq.description: The number of an earlier event that counts.

house.description: The house that becomes an annex: it stands on a lot, and has no annex of its own.

parent.description: The house it exists for: it stands on a lot and is no annex, and not the house itself.

payload.description: A link learned later: the house leaves its lot and stands beside the parent.
